findings.claim: Immediate selection evidence and descendant credit are not the same quantity: the information audit compares geometric nearest-teacher choice against fixed-frame Hungarian RMS with leave-one-batch exclusion over 14 independent batches, and explicitly states it is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, and that nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect.

The compressed-choice excess fixed RMS is small (whole-window mean about 0.081 A, batch-bootstrap CI95 roughly 0.070-0.092 A) relative to the raw fixed RMS (about 0.564 A) and proper-rigid RMS (about 0.529 A), so the selection advantage is a small fraction of total geometric error and cannot be read as a large affinity benefit.

Chosen-teacher score correlations are weak and observational: compressed-choice correlation whole-window mean about 0.102 (CI95 ~0.065-0.140) and full-choice about 0.064 (CI95 ~0.021-0.103); the audit states these are not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor.

Ancestral coverage is thin: of 700 total batch nodes, 349 have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, with at most 2 teachers per batch, so most nodes cannot support a stable within-path credit estimate.

Survival/terminal credit is a different label calculation from final affinity: lineage support declares terminal-credit-mining-1.0 with multiple testing BH jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests and states these are not terminal affinity effects; terminal metadata show one future-resampling node per batch at terminal index 99 (score time 0.99, state time 1.0), outside the observed learning window [0.0,0.5].

The curve-fidelity audit shows the selected 24 continuous features generally fail the declared fidelity rule (relative_node_rmse <= 0.35): every listed feature has relative_node_rmse between about 0.39 and 0.93, and many carry strong sign conflicts (e.g. landmark_16_occupancy5 has 15, landmark_15_occupancy5 and landmark_15_softmin have 10), so last-fit z and last-empirical z frequently disagree in sign.

The curve-support selection rule required absolute integrated z >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857, q < 0.05 and exclusion of the scale floor, selecting 24 features; this is a multiplicity- and coverage-aware filter rather than a point-estimate ranking, and it is the only supplied basis for prioritizing coordinate hypotheses.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only, and the reward view is endpoint_pointcloud with a detached-Hungarian endpoint mean squared distance and pointcloud_delta_A = 1.0 A; no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is permitted.

hypotheses.direction: Rank coordinate hypotheses by adjusted support and fidelity, not by point estimate.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the adjusted-support ranking reproduces the point-estimate ranking exactly, the adjustment adds no prioritization information.
hypotheses.observable: Selected feature set under the declared selection rule versus the top features by whole-window mean.
hypotheses.statement: Prioritizing coordinate regions by multiplicity-adjusted, coverage-aware support (integrated z, batch direction fraction, q) rather than by point-estimate magnitude will select a different and smaller set of regions than ranking raw means alone, because the fidelity audit shows several large-magnitude features fail the relative-RMSE and sign-conflict criteria.

hypotheses.direction: Deprioritize or exclude high-sign-conflict features from any coordinate rule.
hypotheses.falsifier: A feature with many sign conflicts that nonetheless shows consistent batch-direction agreement would weaken this exclusion.
hypotheses.observable: Strong_sign_conflict_nodes count and sign agreement between last_fit_z and last_empirical_z.
hypotheses.statement: Features with many strong sign conflicts (e.g. landmark_16_occupancy5, landmark_15_occupancy5, landmark_15_softmin) are not reproducible coordinate directions and should not be used to steer control, because their last-fit and last-empirical z disagree in sign across nodes.

hypotheses.direction: Treat within-path versus cohort-composition attribution as unresolved.
hypotheses.falsifier: A subset of nodes with >=6 ancestors and consistent teacher assignment would permit a within-path estimate.
hypotheses.observable: Ancestor counts per node and teachers_per_batch_max.
hypotheses.statement: Because most nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and at most 2 teachers per batch, within-path change cannot be separated from changing cohort composition using the supplied credit table alone; the turnover residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect.

hypotheses.direction: Only a fidelity-passing feature may be turned into a temporal-region coordinate intervention.
hypotheses.falsifier: If no selected feature meets the fidelity rule, no registered recipe can express the hypothesis and it stays descriptive.
hypotheses.observable: Relative_node_rmse <= 0.35 and zero strong sign conflicts for the candidate feature.
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned regional attention rule could be expressed through the registered temporal_region recipe (validated absolute contrast changes regional attention at observed score nodes) if a feature passes the fidelity rule; otherwise the finding remains descriptive.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record and survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit, and the immediate-selection versus descendant-credit comparison remains unavailable.
The information audit is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, and its excess-distance metric is nonnegative by construction, so it is not a causal affinity effect.
Teacher score correlations are observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor.
All 24 selected continuous features fail the declared relative_node_rmse <= 0.35 fidelity rule, so no validated time-conditioned contrast fit is available for a coordinate intervention.
Terminal metadata lie outside the observed learning window [0.0,0.5]; no extrapolation beyond observed support is permitted.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed or evaluated.
